findings.source_quote: μετὰ τὸ ἰδεῖν με ταῦτα ἐθαύμαζον ἐν ἐμαυτῷ, ὅτι μεγάλα καὶ ἔνδοξα πράγματα βλέπω.
findings.english_quote: I marveled that I was seeing such great and glorious things.
findings.issue: The simplified sentence omits both the explicit temporal link, “after seeing these things,” and the inward location of Hermas’s marveling, “within myself.” These details establish the private reflection to which the shepherd subsequently responds.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “After seeing these things, I marveled within myself that I was seeing such great and glorious things.”

findings.source_quote: Τί ἐν σεαυτῷ διαλογίζῃ καὶ διαπορῇ, καὶ σεαυτῷ λύπην ἐπισπᾶσαι;
findings.english_quote: Why do you puzzle over these things and make yourself sorrowful?
findings.issue: The question retains puzzlement and self-caused sorrow but drops the distinct activity of reasoning or deliberating and its explicit inward setting. This reduces the shepherd’s rebuke of Hermas’s internal deliberation to puzzlement alone.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “Why do you reason and puzzle within yourself and bring sorrow on yourself?”

summary: The standard edition faithfully represents the selected working Greek across all seven paragraphs. The simplified edition independently preserves the scene, speakers, negations, and instructions, but needs two small restorations to Hermas’s inward reflection. The bounded witness notes do not claim fresh manuscript authentication or exhaustive collation and do not contradict the supplied project reports. Acceptance is limited to this source-based model review; proposed revisions require fresh review.
